headline: Temperature is molecular motion—heat is energy moving from faster-vibrating molecules to slower ones
universal_truth: Energy flows from more to less; understanding direction helps you work with natural forces
fun_facts: Absolute zero (-273.15°C) is the temperature where all molecular motion theoretically stops
You can't feel temperature directly—you feel the rate at which heat leaves or enters your body
Hot water can freeze faster than cold water under certain conditions—the Mpemba effect
discussion_questions: Why does metal feel colder than wood at the same temperature?
How does understanding heat flow change how you think about staying warm or cool?
What other things in life flow from more to less?

hook.script: Touch metal and wood in the same room—the metal feels colder. But they're the same temperature. What you're actually feeling isn't temperature; it's how fast heat leaves your hand. Temperature is stranger than it seems.

cliff.script: We say things 'have' a temperature, as if it's a property like color. But temperature is really about motion. What is heat actually, and why does it always flow in one direction?

options.text: Heat is energy in the form of molecular motion—faster vibration means higher temperature, and heat flows from faster to slower molecules
options.response: Yes. Temperature measures how fast molecules are vibrating. Heat flows from high-energy molecules to low-energy ones until they equalize. That's why hot things cool down.

options.text: Heat is a type of invisible substance that moves between objects
options.response: Scientists once thought this ('caloric'), but heat is actually molecular motion...

fact1.title: Molecular Dance
fact1.script: Atoms and molecules are always moving—vibrating, spinning, bouncing. Temperature measures how energetically they're dancing. At absolute zero, motion would stop. At high temperatures, molecules move frantically.

fact2.title: Conductivity Matters
fact2.script: Metal feels colder than wood because metal conducts heat away from your hand faster. Both are room temperature, but metal steals your heat quickly, wood slowly. You feel heat flow, not temperature.

fact3.title: Heat Always Flows Downhill
fact3.script: Heat only flows from hot to cold—never the reverse, without work. This is the second law of thermodynamics. Understanding this direction helps you work with nature: insulation slows the flow; refrigerators pump against it using energy.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Energy flows from more to less. Temperature teaches that understanding direction helps you work with natural forces. Don't fight the flow—redirect it.

outro.script: That's Day 181—June complete! Tomorrow starts July with where new ideas come from. Until then, notice heat flow around you—warming, cooling, always seeking balance.

growTrack.title: Heat Awareness - Feel the Flow
growTrack.learning_objective: Notice heat transfer in daily life
growTrack.activity: Pay attention to heat flow today: your warm coffee cooling, cold drinks warming, your body heat escaping outdoors. Feel how different materials conduct heat differently. Understanding heat flow helps you stay comfortable with less energy.
